job.title: Environmental Business Partner - Qld
job.description:
Are you an experienced environmental professional who enjoys getting out on site, solving practical challenges and working alongside operational leaders to make a genuine difference?

Our client is Australia's largest vertically integrated construction materials company, and today they are seeking an experienced Environment Business Partner to support their extensive Queensland operations.

This is an opportunity to combine your technical environmental expertise with a highly visible, operationally focused business partnering role, influencing environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement across a diverse network of quarries, concrete batching plants, asphalt operations and recycling facilities.

Reporting to the Senior Environment Business Partner, you will work closely with Quarry Managers, Regional Managers and operational teams, providing practical advice, coaching and guidance to strengthen environmental capability and accountability.
 
This is not a desk-based compliance role.  Success will come from your ability to establish credibility on site, understand operational challenges and translate environmental obligations into practical solutions that support both compliance and business performance.
 
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Partner with operational leaders to strengthen environmental compliance, risk management and site performance.
  • Conduct site inspections, environmental audits and assurance activities, identifying risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Provide practical advice on environmental approvals, licence conditions, legislation and operational requirements.
  • Support environmental monitoring programs, including water, dust, noise, emissions and other site-specific obligations.
  • Coordinate environmental compliance reporting, including annual returns, monitoring results and National Pollutant Inventory (NPI) submissions.
  • Investigate environmental incidents and complaints, identify root causes and support corrective actions.
  • Review environmental management plans, approvals and operating conditions to maintain compliance.
  • Advise operational teams on land disturbance, vegetation clearing, water management and other site activities.
  • Coach and educate site personnel, building environmental capability, ownership and accountability.
  • Work with consultants, regulators and internal stakeholders to resolve environmental matters and support continuous improvement.
  • Contribute to environmental improvement initiatives and the implementation of Boral's broader environmental strategy.
What you will bring to this role:
  • You will be a technically capable environmental professional with the confidence, initiative and interpersonal skills to influence outcomes in a complex operational environment.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
  • Approximately five years or more of environmental experience within heavy industry, mining, quarrying, construction, manufacturing, waste management or a regulatory environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of environmental legislation, approvals, licence conditions and compliance requirements.
  • Practical experience with environmental monitoring, inspections, incident investigations, reporting and risk management.
  • The ability to interpret technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the confidence to advise, coach and influence site and regional management teams.
  • A proactive, self-directed approach, with the ability to prioritise competing activities across multiple locations.
  • Sound commercial judgement and an appreciation of the need to balance environmental compliance with operational realities.
  • Experience working across multiple operational sites, particularly within quarrying, mining or other extractive industries, will be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to environmental regulator engagement, approvals or licence variations would also be advantageous.
  • Importantly, you will enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and taking ownership of delivering outcomes.
Why Join this Icon - So what's in it for you?

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within an established Australian organisation where environmental performance is integral to business operations.

You'll benefit from:
  • Competitive remuneration: $140,000-$160,000 plus super + $17,000 motor vehicle allowance.
  • Variety and autonomy: A diverse portfolio of operational sites presenting interesting technical and environmental challenges.
  • Genuine business influence: Work directly with operational decision-makers, helping shape practical environmental outcomes.
  • Field-based engagement: A balanced mix of site visits, operational collaboration and office-based technical work.
  • Professional development: Broaden your exposure across quarrying, construction materials, manufacturing and recycling operations.
  • Supportive leadership: Work alongside an experienced Senior Environment Business Partner who values initiative, collaboration and getting things done.
  • Long-term opportunity: Join a major Australian business with an extensive operational footprint and ongoing environmental improvement priorities.
Location and Travel
Based in Milton, Brisbane, this role requires regular travel across Queensland to support operational sites.
During the initial three to six months, approximately two nights away from home per week may be required as you develop your understanding of the business, build relationships and become familiar with site operations.
Flexibility is available to work from operational locations where appropriate.
 
Interested?
If you're an experienced environmental professional looking for a role that combines technical expertise, operational engagement and genuine business influence, we'd welcome your application.
 
Apply now by submitting your resume, or contact Louisa on 0459 991 061 for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Business Development Executive - New Business Sales
job.description:
Our client is part of a global leader in water purification and filtration, providing innovative hydration solutions across commercial workplaces, healthcare, education, fitness, hospitality and a broad range of business environments.

With significant growth underway across Australia, they are now looking for a driven Business Development Executive to help grow their presence across Brisbane.

This is a genuine new-business role for someone who enjoys building relationships, creating opportunities and taking ownership of their market.

You’ll have the autonomy to manage your own day, backed by a proven sales process, strong onboarding and an established global organisation.

You don’t necessarily need to come from the water industry or even from a traditional BDM background.

Some of the strongest performers in the business have come from hospitality, retail, sales-adjacent roles and completely different industries. What matters is your ability to connect with people, understand what they need, identify an opportunity and build a relationship that leads to business.

Why this role?
  • $75,000 + Super base salary
  • $15,000 car allowance
  • Uncapped monthly commission
  • OTE circa $125,000
  • Genuine earning potential beyond OTE for strong performers
  • Highly autonomous field-based role
  • Flexibility to manage your own day
  • Significant opportunity across the Brisbane market
  • Comprehensive onboarding and structured sales training
  • Global organisation with established products and strong market presence
  • Opportunity to join the business during a significant growth phase
  • Career development and progression opportunities
  • Supportive and experienced leadership team
 “Once people get through the first six months, they tend not to leave. The longer you’re with us, the easier it becomes and as you build your network, you build your pipeline, and sales bring sales.” — General Manager
 
About the role
This is a highly autonomous, field-based sales role with plenty of scope to make it your own.
A key focus will be developing new business, building your own network and identifying opportunities across a broad commercial market.
You’ll use a mix of prospecting, networking, referrals and face-to-face engagement to build relationships and grow your customer base.
That could include commercial offices, gyms, healthcare environments, warehouses, Early Learning Centers, workplaces and a wide range of other businesses where quality drinking water solutions can add value.

You’ll work with decision-makers to understand their needs, recommend the right solution and manage opportunities through the sales process from initial conversation through to installation.

The role gives you genuine freedom to manage your day and pursue opportunities, while still providing the structure, training and support to help you succeed.

Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities
  • Build and manage your own sales pipeline
  • Engage with prospective customers through phone, networking and face-to-face activity
  • Build strong relationships with business owners and commercial decision-makers
  • Understand customer needs and recommend appropriate solutions
  • Conduct customer meetings, product demonstrations and presentations
  • Negotiate and close new sales opportunities
  • Manage opportunities through the sales process from first contact to installation
  • Maintain accurate customer and pipeline information
  • Work closely with internal teams to ensure a positive customer experience
  • Develop relationships that support repeat business and referrals
  • Take ownership of your market and identify new areas for growth
About you
You may already be working as a Sales Representative, Sales Consultant, Territory Sales Representative, Business Development Executive, Account Executive or BDM.

But your job title is not the most important part.

You may equally come from retail sales, hospitality, field sales, promotional sales or have previously run your own business.

The business has successfully hired people from a wide range of backgrounds because the common denominator is not industry experience, but it is attitude, commercial awareness and the ability to connect with people.

You’ll be someone who enjoys meeting new people, building rapport and identifying opportunities.

You are self-motivated, commercially minded and comfortable managing your own time and priorities.

You like having ownership of your results and the freedom to build your market in a way that works.

You will also be open to learning and comfortable working within a proven sales process that gives you the tools and support to succeed.

What you will bring
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • Confidence engaging with new customers
  • A proactive approach to developing new business
  • Ability to build rapport quickly and understand customer needs
  • Strong self-motivation and personal accountability
  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of the sales process
  • Confidence working autonomously in the field
  • Ability to manage your own time, activity and pipeline
  • Resilience and a results-focused mindset
  • Willingness to learn and work within a proven sales process
  • Previous sales experience highly regarded, although the right capability may come from outside traditional B2B sales
The environment
This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the market rather than sitting behind a desk all day.

You’ll spend your time meeting customers, building relationships, developing opportunities and growing your network.

Our client offers genuine autonomy, supported by a comprehensive induction, product training and a structured approach to helping new starters build confidence and momentum.

The Brisbane market offers significant growth potential, with a broad range of industries and customers still available to develop.

At $75K base + $15K car allowance + uncapped commission, the advertised OTE is around $125K.

Importantly, that is not an earnings ceiling.

For people who consistently build relationships, create opportunities and convert business, there is genuine scope to earn considerably more.

If you are looking for a role where you can own your day, build your own market and be directly rewarded for the results you create, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your application including a current resume.

job.title: Environmental Business Partner
job.description:
Our client is an established Australian business in the construction materials sector. This is an opportunity to apply your environmental expertise across a diverse operational portfolio and help site teams turn compliance requirements into practical action.

Based at Port Melbourne and reporting to the Senior Environmental Business Partner, you will provide hands-on environmental advice and support across multiple operational sites. The role includes regular site travel within greater Melbourne and visits to regional Victoria and Tasmania as required.

You will combine field inspections with office-based planning, reporting and stakeholder engagement. The role offers an indicative mix of one to two days in Port Melbourne, one day working from home and the remaining time at operational sites, depending on business needs.

About the Role
  • Partner with site managers and operations teams to understand environmental obligations, manage risks and improve performance.
  • Undertake site inspections, environmental compliance verifications and aspects and impacts register reviews, and track corrective actions through to completion.
  • Maintain environmental management plans, registers and operating conditions, and support ground disturbance processes.
  • Coordinate monitoring programs, including water and dust, and review, analyse and report data within required timeframes.
  • Support regulator liaison, regulatory reporting, incident investigations and the management of environmental complaints.
  • Coach site teams, deliver environmental education and support regional improvement plans and the organisation’s environmental strategy.
About You
You are an experienced environmental practitioner who is comfortable in both a site environment and an office. You build credibility with operational teams, negotiate practical solutions and know when an issue needs to be escalated.
  • A relevant environmental tertiary qualification, preferably Environmental Science or Environmental Engineering.
  • At least five years of relevant environmental experience in heavy industry or a regulator environment. Construction, mining, manufacturing, waste and operational facility experience are valued, as is relevant consulting experience.
  • A track record of providing practical environmental support in complex environments, with sound knowledge of regulations, management systems and processes.
  • Experience with site inspections, monitoring, environmental reporting and stakeholder engagement, including regulators.
  • Strong communication and organisation skills, a pragmatic approach and the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple sites.
  • Confidence using environmental information systems and technology, with an interest in improving how work is done.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to operational sites across Victoria and Tasmania.
Breadth of experience is particularly valuable. If you have a strong construction background and experience in other operational or consulting settings, this role offers an opportunity to bring that knowledge into an ongoing operational portfolio.
What is on offer
  • Up to $150,000 base salary plus superannuation and a $17,000 motor vehicle allowance.
  • A permanent full-time role with varied site exposure and support from an experienced Senior Environmental Business Partner.
  • A Port Melbourne base with secure parking, flexibility in work location around business needs and one day working from home.
  • The opportunity to broaden your experience across a major Australian construction materials business.
How to Apply
If you’re ready to shape the future of environmental practice and build capability within a national brand known for excellence and growth, apply today with your cover letter and resume or contact Nicki at Hinchen Recruitment Group in confidence to learn more.

job.title: Regional Operations Manager - Quarries
job.description:
REGIONAL OPERATIONS MANAGER – QUARRIES

* Lead nine quarry operations across a large and diverse regional portfolio
* Take ownership of an approximately $95 million P&L and two million tonnes of annual sales
* Deliver significant operational, asset, resource development and capital priorities


Your next opportunity!
This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished quarrying leader to take responsibility for a significant regional portfolio within one of Australia’s leading construction materials organisations.

Reporting directly to the General Manager, you will lead nine quarry operations across Queensland and the Northern Territory, supported by experienced Quarry Managers and specialist leaders across assets, logistics, finance, commercial, property, sales and safety.

With an approximately $95 million P&L, annual sales of around two million tonnes and a substantial program of operational and capital investment, you will have genuine scope to shape performance, strengthen operational consistency and deliver lasting improvement across a diverse and commercially important portfolio.

The Opportunity
Your portfolio includes operations across Cairns, Townsville, Mackay, Wide Bay, Toowoomba and Darwin.
The role may be based in Brisbane, Townsville or another practical Queensland location, with Mackay, Cairns and the Wide Bay-Burnett region also open for consideration. Regular travel across the portfolio will be required.

You will lead a group of Quarry Managers with varying levels of operational, commercial and leadership experience. Your role will be to establish credibility quickly, create a consistent operating cadence and ensure each site receives the right level of leadership, challenge and support.

Key priorities will include:
· Securing the long-term continuity of quarry resources and raw materials
· Improving fixed-plant productivity, reliability and cost-per-unit performance
· Delivering significant operational and capital projects
· Establishing consistent KPIs, operating metrics and performance disciplines
· Strengthening accountability and capability across the Quarry Manager group
· Implementing and embedding key quarry safety initiatives
· Maintaining safe, compliant and environmentally responsible operations

Planned and potential investment includes a new primary crushing circuit, significant fixed-plant development, sand quarry asset replacement and a range of resource development, stripping, mobile equipment and site infrastructure projects.

Your Responsibilities
You will be accountable for:
· Providing operational leadership across nine quarrying operations
· Leading, coaching and developing the portfolio’s Quarry Managers
· Managing an approximately $95 million regional P&L
· Delivering production, safety, cost, margin and operational performance outcomes
· Driving fixed-plant and mobile-equipment optimisation
· Developing business cases and leading operational input into capital projects
· Identifying and prioritising replacement, continuity and growth investment
· Ensuring long-term resource availability and operational continuity
· Building greater consistency and standardisation across the regional network
· Partnering with finance, commercial, assets, logistics, property, sales and safety teams
· Managing relationships with regulators, councils, communities and other stakeholders
· Maintaining strong site visibility through regular regional travel

What you will bring
This role requires more than broad heavy-industry leadership. You will need the technical and operational credibility to engage experienced Quarry Managers, understand what is happening beneath the headline numbers and challenge performance constructively.
You will bring:
· An open Site Senior Executive (SSE) qualification, or the background and capability to obtain the required Queensland qualification quickly
· Substantial operational leadership experience within quarrying, aggregates or a closely aligned environment
· Previous responsibility for a large quarry or multiple quarry operations
· A deep understanding of safe, productive and commercially successful quarry operations
· Strong financial literacy and previous accountability for operational P&Ls, budgets and forecasts
· Experience developing capital business cases and delivering complex operational or asset projects
· Knowledge of fixed-plant optimisation, crushing operations, mobile equipment and resource development
· Demonstrated success leading experienced operational managers across multiple locations
· Strong knowledge of quarry safety, environmental and regulatory requirements
· The ability to interpret operational and financial data and turn it into decisive action
· A proactive leadership style and the confidence to take ownership without waiting for direction
· The flexibility to travel regularly across Queensland and the Northern Territory

Applicants from mining or mineral-processing environments may be considered where they can demonstrate highly transferable quarrying knowledge. However, direct experience within quarries, sand or aggregates will be strongly preferred.

Why join?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a quarrying portfolio with genuine scale, complexity and organisational visibility.

You will have significant autonomy, direct access to the General Manager and the opportunity to influence substantial operational and capital investment. You will also be supported by an established team of specialists across finance, assets, logistics, commercial, property and safety.

The organisation is seeking a leader who can move confidently between portfolio strategy and site-level operations, someone who knows when to step into the detail, when to challenge and when to empower others.

If you combine deep quarrying knowledge with commercial discipline, authentic leadership and the ability to turn priorities into action, we would welcome a confidential discussion.

For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, please contact Lorraine Thompson 0431 767 528 or simply follow the link and apply now. All enquiries and applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

job.title: Quarry Manager
job.description:
An opportunity is available for an experienced Quarry Manager to take responsibility for a major hard rock quarry operation in the Gold Coast hinterland.
Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will lead all aspects of site operations, with responsibility for safety, production, financial performance, people leadership and ongoing site development.
This is a hands-on leadership position requiring a strong understanding of quarry operations, commercial performance and the ability to build an engaged, accountable team. You will play an important role in ensuring the quarry operates safely and efficiently while meeting production targets, customer requirements and broader business objectives.

What You'll Be Responsible For
  • Leading the day-to-day management of quarry operations, including production, crushing and processing, drill and blast activities and fixed plant performance.
  • Driving a proactive safety culture and ensuring environmental, legislative and regulatory obligations are consistently met.
  • Managing operational budgets, costs and overall site profitability, with full accountability for P&L performance.
  • Developing and delivering production plans to achieve agreed output, quality, efficiency and financial targets.
  • Leading, coaching and developing employees and contractors to build a capable, motivated and high-performing workforce.
  • Working collaboratively with the Sales team to meet customer expectations, support revenue growth and ensure reliable product supply.
  • Overseeing maintenance planning, capital expenditure initiatives and future quarry development requirements.
  • Identifying opportunities to improve productivity, reduce operating costs and strengthen operational performance.
  • Building effective working relationships with customers, regulators, internal stakeholders and the surrounding community.
  • Ensuring the quarry maintains compliance with all relevant operating licences, statutory requirements and industry standards.
What You Will Bring

To be successful in this role, you will have demonstrated experience managing operations within the quarrying, mining or broader extractive industries, together with strong leadership and commercial management capabilities.
You will also offer:
  • A solid technical understanding of hard rock quarry operations, including crushing, screening and materials processing.
  • Experience leading operational teams and creating a workplace culture focused on safety, accountability and performance.
  • A sound working knowledge of the Mining and Quarrying Safety and Health Act and associated Regulations.
  • Proven financial management capability, including budgeting, cost control, forecasting and P&L responsibility.
  • Experience implementing operational improvements that deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Current Site Senior Executive (SSE) appointment or the ability to obtain and maintain the required SSE practising certificate.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to develop productive relationships across a range of stakeholders.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach to managing operational challenges and making decisions.
  • The confidence to work independently while maintaining alignment with wider business priorities.
  • A current unrestricted driver's licence.
What's In It for You?

This position offers the opportunity to take ownership of an established, strategically important quarry operation supplying materials to major infrastructure and construction projects across South East Queensland.
Benefits include:
  • A competitive remuneration package aligned with your experience and capability.
  • Performance-based incentives and a Tool of Trade vehicle.
  • The opportunity to manage a significant hard rock quarry operation within the national network.
  • A leadership role supporting infrastructure development across one of Queensland's key growth regions.
  • Access to experienced operational leaders, technical specialists and established business support functions.
  • Opportunities to further develop your leadership and technical expertise within a large, integrated quarrying business.
  • Ongoing professional development, training and longer-term career progression opportunities.
  • The autonomy to make operational decisions and have a genuine impact on site performance.
If you are an experienced quarrying professional who enjoys leading people, improving operational performance and taking ownership of business outcomes, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within a well-established operation. job.title: Project Manager Concrete
job.description:
Project Manager – Major Concrete Operations
Sunshine Coast
Highly competitive Salary – paid relocation costs considered
  
Take ownership of the concrete operations supporting one of the Sunshine Coast’s most significant infrastructure projects and help establish the next operation from the ground up.
Our client is one of Australia’s leading construction materials organisations, with an extensive network of concrete, quarry and operational sites across the country and their people and products support major residential, commercial and civil infrastructure projects, helping to build stronger and more sustainable communities.
Based near Cooroy, you will lead the onsite concrete operations supporting a complex dam improvement project. You will manage plant performance, people, customer relationships, budgets and production delivery, while also helping prepare for an additional project operation at Coolum.
This is not a desk-based project-management position. You will be visible on site, working alongside your team, resolving operational issues and ensuring concrete is produced safely, consistently and in line with demanding project schedules.
This is a permanent position offering exposure to a strong pipeline of major projects beyond the current program.

Your next opportunity
Reporting to the Major Projects Manager for South East Queensland Concrete, you will initially take responsibility for an established onsite operation at Lake Macdonald.

As the project develops, you will also play an important role in establishing and staffing the next concrete operation at Coolum, with the potential to oversee multiple project sites across the Sunshine Coast.

You will lead four direct reports and coordinate approximately 10–15 drivers, working closely with the principal construction contractor, technical teams, suppliers and internal stakeholders.

The environment is fast-moving and highly accountable. Production volumes are significant, customer expectations are high and reliable plant performance is critical to the successful delivery of the broader infrastructure program.
  
Your responsibilities
  • Lead safe, reliable and efficient concrete operations across major project sites
  • Manage daily production requirements against changing project schedules and customer demand
  • Coordinate concrete orders, batching activities, testing and technical support
  • Maintain plant availability and coordinate preventative and reactive maintenance
  • Lead, coach and develop production employees and drivers
  • Create an engaged, accountable and safety-focused site culture
  • Conduct toolbox talks and ensure employees and contractors follow site requirements
  • Build strong working relationships with construction partners, engineers and other stakeholders
  • Respond quickly and professionally to customer concerns and operational issues
  • Manage site expenditure, labour costs, budgets, forecasts and operational performance
  • Monitor production, service, safety and plant-performance targets
  • Drive continuous improvement across plant operations, systems and processes
  • Support recruitment, onboarding and workforce planning for the new project operation
  • Assist with concrete batching and front-end loader operations when required
  • Ensure compliance with all safety, environmental and quality requirements
  
About you
You are an experienced operational leader who is equally comfortable talking with production employees on the plant floor and meeting with engineers and senior project stakeholders.
You remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly and take ownership when production priorities change or problems arise. You understand that strong customer relationships must be supported by safe operations, reliable equipment and consistent delivery.
You will ideally bring:
  • Operational leadership experience within concrete production or a closely related environment
  • A sound understanding of concrete batching, production processes and quality requirements
  • Experience leading plant-based teams in a safety-critical environment
  • Strong customer and stakeholder-management capability
  • The confidence to work directly with construction managers, engineers and project representatives
  • Experience managing production schedules, labour, costs, budgets and operational targets
  • Practical knowledge of plant maintenance, reliability and asset utilisation
  • The ability to balance competing priorities in a high-volume operation
  • A visible and hands-on leadership style
  • Front-end loader operating experience and ideally a current front-end loader ticket
  • A valid Construction White Card
  • A current driver’s license and clean driving record
  
Experience within civil construction, aggregates, quarrying or another heavy production environment may also be considered where you can demonstrate meaningful exposure to concrete operations.
Formal project-management or engineering qualifications are welcome but are not essential. Your operational experience, leadership capability and understanding of concrete production will carry greater weight.
If you do not currently hold a front-end loader ticket but have relevant operational experience and are willing and able to obtain one, we would still welcome a conversation.

Why this opportunity stands out
This role offers considerably more scope than managing a single permanent concrete plant.
You will work at the centre of a significant civil infrastructure project where your decisions directly influence production continuity, customer outcomes and project delivery. You will inherit an established operation, help shape a new site and have the opportunity to build and lead its team.
You will also receive:
  • A permanent, full-time position not a project-based contract
  • An attractive salary package including a tool of the trade vehicle plus relocation assistance if required.
  • A predominantly Monday-to-Friday day-shift roster
  • Exposure to complex, high-profile infrastructure delivery
  • The opportunity to establish and grow additional concrete operations
  • An accessible manager who encourages autonomy and open communication
  • Really positive culture on site
  • Strong technical, safety and operational support

job.title: Project Director | Major Capital Upgrade | Southern Highlands NSW
job.description:
Project Director | Major Capital Upgrade | Southern Highlands NSW


Hinchen Recruitment Group is partnering with a leading Australian construction materials business to appoint a Project Director for a m
major infrastructure upgrade at its NSW Southern Highlands location.


This is a business critical investment that will secure the long-term supply of raw materials to its operations. The programme includes a new primary crusher, screening and conveying systems, an enclosed stacker reclaimer, and associated power, rail and site infrastructure. The completed facilities are designed to deliver 4 million tonnes of crushed rock each year.


The appeal of this role is the point at which you will join. Key equipment sourcing is under way, but the delivery structure and contracting approach are still being shaped. Our client wants an experienced leader who will take ownership, bring sound commercial judgement and build the team required to deliver the project successfully.

What's in it for you?
  • A project with real scale and purpose: lead an investment of approximately $100m that is central to the future of the operation.
  • The opportunity to make it your own: influence the contracting model, establish the project controls and help determine the structure of your delivery team.
  • High visibility and genuine accountability: work closely with senior leaders and take the project through to commissioning and operational handover.
  • An attractive package: remuneration will reflect your experience, with flexibility up to circa $320k for an exceptional candidate.
  • A Southern Highlands location: enjoy a site based role in one of NSW's most appealing regions. Relocation can be discussed.
The role
You will be accountable for project scope, cost, schedule, safety and quality. One of your most important challenges will be integrating internationally sourced equipment with local construction and installation packages, while works proceed alongside an operating site.
You will develop the delivery plan and contracting strategy, build and lead a multidisciplinary team, manage major suppliers and contractors, and oversee construction, commissioning and handover. You will be supported by established engineering, procurement, operations, legal and planning teams.


About you
You have personally led a major capital project involving crushing, processing plant or comparable bulk materials handling infrastructure. You may come from quarrying, mining, cement, minerals processing or another heavy industrial environment.


You will bring strong experience in contract strategy and administration, managing multiple specialist contractors, resolving commercial and technical interfaces, and delivering works within a live operation. You are equally credible on site and in an executive project review, and you know how to build a team that takes ownership of delivery.


An engineering degree or related qualification is required. 


This is a site based fixed term opportunity, with the project currently expected to run through to approximately June 2029.
